synthesis: GenerateOrgCache runs every 4h and dispatches a per-org Bus::batch([CacheOrgHotlistClients, CacheOrgHotlistLienholders]) on the {low} queue. Each job calls Org::getHotlistClients()/getHotlistLienholders() (app/Models/Org.php:185,202), which wrap `SELECT name,id FROM orgs WHERE id IN (SELECT DISTINCT client_org_id FROM hotlist WHERE org_id=? AND client_org_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY name` in cache()->remember(...,endOfDay) against the zod READ replica. For a small number of large-hotlist orgs the query exceeds the replica's statement_timeout (SQLSTATE 57014); the exception is thrown BEFORE remember() can put(), so the cache never warms and the identical query re-runs every tick (12x 2026-07-22, 20x 2026-07-23). CRITICAL: this is a RECURRENCE. DEV-1898 (Done, commit c744f887) already pushed DISTINCT+WHERE NOT NULL into the subquery and removed the PHP-side pluck()->unique() for BOTH methods — that is exactly today's code. So the query-shape rewrite alone was insufficient. The residual cost is the missing composite index: public.hotlist has only single-column ix_hotlist_org_id / ix_hotlist_client_org_id / ix_hotlist_lienholder_org_id (+ (org_id,status,...)), NO composite (org_id,client_org_id) / (org_id,lienholder_org_id), so Postgres must heap-visit every org-matching row to build the DISTINCT list. That index is the durable fix, but public.hotlist schema is owned by the vendor package insight-lpr/laravel-zod-migrations (okf/concepts/data-architecture.md:135), and platform's only zod-connection migration is guarded config('app.env')!=='production' — so platform CANNOT ship a production-effective index. The realistic platform-only deliverable is resilience: catch 57014 in the Org getters (not just the jobs — ~9 synchronous Filament/console callers hit the same query on cache-miss and risk user-facing 500s), degrade to an empty Collection, and log via the existing HasRetryQuery convention. Exactly how far the platform mitigation should go (catch-only vs a bounded SET LOCAL statement_timeout that tries to actually warm the cache) and the degraded-UX/negative-cache tradeoffs are genuine open decisions for the human.

scope.summary: Platform-only resilience for Org::getHotlistClients()/getHotlistLienholders(): catch the QueryException(57014) statement-timeout, degrade gracefully to an empty Collection (protecting both the two warm-cache jobs and the ~9 synchronous UI/console callers), and log/meter via the existing db-error channel + logDatadogCount('clarity.query_timeout') convention. The durable fix (composite index on public.hotlist) is cross-repo (vendor laravel-zod-migrations) and OUT OF SCOPE for this platform PR — track as a companion, likely under epic DEV-2202. The exact mitigation shape (catch-only vs bounded SET LOCAL statement_timeout, negative-cache-on-failure, degraded-state UX) is BLOCKED on human input.

questions.q: SCOPE: Is DEV-2220's platform deliverable the resilience mitigation ONLY (catch 57014 in the Org getters + graceful empty degrade + org-scoped logging), with the durable composite index tracked as a cross-repo companion (vendor laravel-zod-migrations / DBA), likely under epic DEV-2202? Or do you want something more/different in this PR?
questions.answer: Resilience-only. Dalton: 'We cannot change any database schema.' The composite index is OFF THE TABLE entirely — no migration, no cross-repo companion, no schema change of any kind. Platform ships graceful degradation only, accepting that affected large-hotlist orgs' client/lienholder dropdowns degrade to empty until the underlying data/perf changes out of band.

questions.q: APPROACH: Catch-only (stop the error storm; cache stays cold until the index lands — dropdowns show empty for affected orgs), OR also add a bounded `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` (in a transaction, no connection leak) to give the query a real chance to complete and warm the cache? Catch-only is simpler but doesn't fix the user-visible empty dropdown; the bounded timeout tries to actually warm it but its sufficiency is unverifiable without prod EXPLAIN.
questions.answer: SUPERSEDED by the 2026-07-23 pure-CH pivot. Original decision was catch-only on Postgres; mid-review Dalton reconsidered ('are we covering up the error?'), and after a ClickHouse-source investigation chose PURE-CH: read DISTINCT client/lienholder id+name from clarity.hotlist (ClickHouse) instead of the slow Postgres read-replica whereIn(subquery). Keep cache()->flexible() (stale-while-revalidate) + a resilience catch (now on LaravelClickhouseEloquent ClickhouseException, since the query no longer hits Postgres). No PG schema change; the composite-index / Jeff-Cobb path is dropped as moot. Live-verified the CH name columns are ~99.8%+ populated.

questions.q: NEGATIVE CACHE: On timeout, leave the cache key unset (every subsequent call/tick re-runs the expensive failing query — replica load), or write a short-TTL negative cache (e.g. empty for 10-15 min) to bound repeated replica load at the cost of an empty dropdown during that window?
questions.answer: Leave cache unset. Catch AROUND cache()->remember() so a failure is never persisted; a recovering org repopulates on the next successful call. (Consequence Dalton accepted: callers re-attempt the query on each cache-miss.)

questions.q: DEGRADED UX: Is a silently-empty client/lienholder dropdown acceptable for an affected org, or should there be a visible 'temporarily unavailable' degraded state (matching HasRetryQuery's empty-state pattern)? Also: have real users actually hit page-level 500s here, or has this only shown up in the background-job logs so far?
questions.answer: Silently empty. On timeout the getters return an empty Collection and dropdowns/filters simply show no options (matches existing cold-cache behavior). No visible degraded-state indicator — minimal, consistent change across all call sites.

questions.q: DBA/INFRA (informational, needed for Q2): Does the zod read replica enforce a stricter statement_timeout than the primary? What per-statement timeout value is safe for the warm job? And what is the process for landing the composite index in production (vendor-repo PR + who applies it; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY to avoid locking the large table)?
questions.answer: Moot given the decisions above: no schema change (so no index-deploy process needed) and catch-only (so no bounded statement_timeout value needed). Replica statement_timeout config stays an infra detail outside this PR.

questions.q: Is the pre-existing whereNotNull('client_org_id') in getHotlistClients() worth removing as dead code?
questions.answer: It is a functional no-op — public.hotlist.client_org_id is NOT NULL in the vendor schema, so it filters nothing. Safe to leave or remove; cosmetic only.

questions.q: Should the fix live in the two Org model methods or only in the two jobs?
questions.answer: In the Org model methods. The jobs are thin one-line wrappers; the same two methods are called synchronously from ~9 Filament resources/widgets/pages/console command (HitsResource, HotlistResource, MissedOpportunityResource, AlertSettingsForm, ClientTable, IndividualClientAnalytics::mount, HasStatDrillDown, CreateMissedOpportunityAlertSettings), so a job-only catch would leave those request paths exposed to the same uncaught timeout on cache-miss.

questions.q: Is this a regression of DEV-1898's fix?
questions.answer: No. Diffing commit c744f887 confirms the current app/Models/Org.php is exactly what DEV-1898 shipped (DISTINCT+WHERE NOT NULL pushed into the subquery). DEV-2220 is the same fix hitting its scaling limit for large-hotlist orgs — a recurrence, not a regression.

Not formally linked in Jira, but DEV-2202 (To Do) groups pg-read-replica statement timeouts and lists CacheOrgHotlistClients among affected jobs. Treat as the likely tracking epic for the cross-repo index fix; do not assume a formal link exists.

gate_reason: All material questions answered by Dalton 2026-07-23 (interview folded in). FINAL DECISION: platform ships resilience-only — NO database schema change of any kind (no index, no migration, no cross-repo companion). Catch SQLSTATE 57014 specifically around cache()->remember() in Org::getHotlistClients()/getHotlistLienholders(), log via the HasRetryQuery convention (db-error channel + logDatadogCount with org_id), return an empty Collection uncached; let other QueryExceptions propagate. Silently-empty degraded UX. The cross-repo index blocker is dissolved because the index is explicitly out of bounds — the durable-perf fix is out of band and out of scope.
